notes: porter declared unbuildable after 1 attempt(s): The recursion program's provable body IS the in-guest Jolt verifier: it deserializes a JoltVerifierPreprocessing<F, Curve, PCS>, a proof count, then N RV64IMACProof + JoltDevice pairs, and runs RV64IMACVerifier::verify(). That computation cannot be expressed without jolt-core, which has no no_std path: (1) jolt-core/src/lib.rs carries no #![no_std] attribute at the crate root, so it is unconditionally a std crate and cannot compile for riscv64imac-unknown-none-elf; (2) the only feature that exposes the verifier, jolt-core's `minimal`, is defined as ["ark-ec/std", "ark-ff/std", "ark-std/std", "ark-ff/asm", "rayon"] — it force-enables std on every arkworks dependency and pulls in rayon (OS threads), so default-features=false cannot dislodge it; (3) jolt-sdk gates the verifier behind `guest-verifier = ["guest-std", "dep:common", "jolt-core/minimal"]`, and guest-std resolves to zeroos-std -> zeroos-runtime-musl plus postcard/use-std and serde/std. There is no composition of guest-verifier with guest-nostd/zeroos-runtime-nostd. Porting would therefore require flipping the template guest to std/musl mode, which is explicitly forbidden because it changes the study target. Corroborating evidence that this program is std-by-design rather than incidentally std: the corpus guest's lib.rs has its `#![cfg_attr(feature = "guest", no_std)]` line deliberately commented out, the host calls program.set_std(true) for recursion-guest (vs set_std(false) for the fibonacci/muldiv inner guests), the body uses std::io::Cursor in the hot path, and guest/Cargo.toml requests jolt-sdk features ["guest-verifier", "thread", "random"] — `thread` (zeroos scheduler-cooperative) and `random` (zeroos rng-lcg entropy) are both barred from a no_std deterministic guest. This is essential-OS std in the hot path, not scaffolding std or dependency-default std, so no feature-flag or alloc-repoint fix applies. Lifting only part of the body (e.g. dropping the verify() call) would change the algorithm, which is also forbidden. Secondary, non-decisive obstacles: the guest depends on two build.rs-generated files (src/embedded_bytes.rs and src/provable_macro.rs) absent from the source tree, and its provable_with_config! macro emits its own #[jolt::provable(...)] attribute with heap_size=134217728/max_trace_length=67108864, which conflicts with the template's frozen attribute line. No files were modified; the scaffold is left in its original template state for the next candidate.
